pull.title: KAFKA-21273: Make each streams assignment refiner call cheaper
pull.body:
`AssignmentRefinerImpl.refine()` runs on every streams group heartbeat. This PR makes a call cheaper without changing the intermediate assignment it derives. Each commit is one optimization and can be reviewed on its own:

1. Return the target assignment right after the case analysis when it stages no migration.
2. Walk every task fewer times: count process load in the index walk, find borrowed standby conflicts through the target standby holders, and build that lookup only when it is read.
3. Sort only the decisions, not every stateful target active task.
4. Skip counting active tasks when the refiner returns the target assignment itself.
5. Resolve the stateful subtopologies once per call instead of per (member, subtopology) entry.
6. Find the tasks not on their target owner first, and return before indexing when there are none. This assumes the target assignment names one member per active task, as the rest of the refiner already does.
7. Compare task IDs directly instead of building a comparator chain per comparison.
8. Index only the tasks not on their target owner; the process load still counts every task.
9. Build the target standby holders only for those tasks.
10. Patch members copy-on-write instead of copying every patched member in full.
11. Keep borrowed and parked migrations in hash sets instead of tree sets.
12. Count active tasks only for members whose tasks differ from the target assignment.
13. Build the state-on-disk lookup only when the case analysis asks for it.

Besides the unit tests, each step was checked against the previous refiner on 20,000 random groups, with identical results.

`AssignmentRefinerBenchmark.refinerImpl`, 1,000 members, 5,000 stateful tasks, one standby, MIXED lag, budget 2, µs per call:

| Migrating | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 0% | 4,151 | 151 |
| 1% | 4,345 | 767 |
| 50% | 6,032 | 2,567 |
| 100% | 6,923 | 3,367 |

commit.message:
KAFKA-21273: Skip the refiner's later passes when no migration is staged

When the case analysis stages no migration, the warm-up plan, the standby
filter and the assembly cannot change the target assignment: warm-up tasks,
borrowed standbys and withheld standbys all follow from a staged migration,
and a granted task needs no patch. Return the target assignment right after
the case analysis in that case, which saves two walks over every member's
target standby tasks on each refinement of a settled group.

KAFKA-21273: Walk every task fewer times in the refiner's index and standby passes

The refiner walked every member's stateful active, standby and warm-up
tasks twice per refinement: once to index the current assignment, and again
in indexProcessLoad to count each process's stateful tasks, allocating a
TaskId for every task only to count it. The per-process stateful task and
member counts are now taken inside the indexing walk and carried as
CurrentAssignmentIndex.processLoad, and analyzeTasks, planWarmups,
bestCopyToPromote and loadAfterGrants read them from the index. The counts
use an explicit counter rather than the size of a per-process held-task
set, so the loads stay identical even if a process ever held a task in two
roles.

To find which target standby placement a borrowed migration holds back,
indexStandbyConflicts walked every member's target standby tasks and kept
only the borrowed ones. It now looks up the target standby holders of each
borrowed task in the inversion analyzeTasks already uses. The lookup yields
the same (member, task) pairs, and neither result depends on the visiting
order: the kept member is the smallest member ID, and the already
undelivered tasks form a set.

That inversion was built on every refinement, although only
bestCopyToPromote and indexStandbyConflicts read it, and a refinement of a
group whose stateful tasks are all on their target owners reaches neither.
TargetStandbyHolders now builds it on the first holdersOf lookup and keeps
it for the rest of the refinement; the map is reachable only through
holdersOf.

The intermediate assignment is unchanged.

KAFKA-21273: Sort only the refiner's decisions, not every target active task

analyzeTasks inverted the target assignment into a TreeMap from each
stateful task to its target active owner, so that it visited the tasks in
task order and its staged migrations and granted tasks came out in that
order. Building the TreeMap cost a comparison-based insert for every
stateful task in the group, although most of them are already on their
target owner and produce no decision.

Build the inversion as a HashMap instead, and sort the two decision lists
by task before returning them. They hold only the tasks that are not on
their target owner.

The result is unchanged. Each task's decision reads only the indexed
current assignment, the target standby holders, the members and their
heartbeat versions, and appends to one of the two lists, so it does not
depend on the order the tasks are visited in. Each list holds a task at
most once, so sorting it by task gives the order the TreeMap gave. A target
assignment that names a task as active on two members keeps the same owner
as before, since both maps are filled by the same puts in the same order.

KAFKA-21273: Skip counting active tasks when the target assignment comes back

GroupMetadataManager checks every refined assignment with
AssignmentRefiner.preservesActiveTaskCount, which counts the active tasks
of every member in both the target and the refined assignment. The
built-in refiners return the target assignment itself whenever nothing is
held back, which is every call in a settled group, and a map has as many
active tasks as itself.

preservesActiveTaskCount now returns true without counting when the
refined assignment is the target assignment object.

KAFKA-21273: Resolve the refiner's stateful subtopologies once per call

Every pass of AssignmentRefinerImpl asked, for each (member, subtopology)
entry it visited, whether the subtopology is stateful, and each answer was a
lookup in the sorted subtopology map followed by a check of its changelog
topics. With 1000 members and 100 subtopologies that is tens of thousands of
tree lookups per refinement.

refine() now builds the set of stateful subtopology IDs once, from the same
map with the same test, and the passes test membership in that set. The set
holds exactly the subtopologies the old test accepted, so the derivation is
unchanged.

KAFKA-21273: Find the refiner's misplaced tasks before indexing the group

AssignmentRefinerImpl.refine() indexed the members' current assignment and
looked up the target standby holders of every task before the case
analysis, which then mapped every stateful target active task to its
target owner and skipped each task whose active holder was that owner. A
settled group, where every stateful task runs on its target owner, paid for
all of that on every heartbeat and decided nothing.

The new misplacedTasks walks the target assignment's stateful active tasks
once and keeps those their target owner does not hold as an active task
yet, with that owner; a task already in place costs one lookup and
allocates nothing. When no task is misplaced, refine() returns the target
assignment before indexing anything. Otherwise the case analysis walks
only the misplaced tasks.

The derivation is unchanged for a target assignment that names one member
for each active task, which the rest of the refiner already assumes. The
reconciler grants an active task only when no member holds it as active,
so a task has at most one active holder, and the target owner holds a task
exactly when it is the task's active holder: the test the case analysis
used to skip it.

KAFKA-21273: Compare task IDs without building a comparator per call

TaskId.compareTo built a comparator chain from two method references on
every call. The refiner sorts its decisions and keeps the warm-up plan in
sorted maps and sets, and the task assignors sort tasks too, so the chain
was built again for every comparison they made.

compareTo now compares the subtopology IDs and then the partitions
directly, which is the same order. TaskIdTest checks that order, including
that partitions compare as numbers rather than as strings.

KAFKA-21273: Index only the refiner's misplaced tasks

AssignmentRefinerImpl.indexCurrentAssignment recorded the active holder,
the copies and the on-disk reports of every stateful task the members
hold, although the passes after it only look up tasks that are not on
their target owner yet. It now takes those misplaced tasks and records
only them, so a refinement in which few tasks move no longer pays for
indexing the whole group.

Two results still cover every task and are worked out in the same walk
over the members: each process's load, now the sum of the sizes of the
members' stateful partition sets, and the members restoring one of their
active tasks, which the warm-up planning used to read off the index and
which is now collected from each member's own offset reports. A reported
task counts as on disk when no member of its process holds it, which is
now looked up in the index instead of in a set of every task each
process holds.

The intermediate assignment is unchanged: every task the later passes
look up is a misplaced one, the load counts the same placements, and a
member is restoring an active task exactly when it reports an offset for
one of its own stateful active tasks, since a task has at most one active
holder.

KAFKA-21273: Look up the target standby holders of misplaced tasks only

TargetStandbyHolders inverted the whole target assignment into a map from
every stateful task to the members named as its standby holders. Its
readers only ask about tasks that are not on their target owner yet:
bestCopyToPromote ranks the copies of a task the case analysis decides,
and the standby filter looks up borrowed migrations, which are staged
ones and therefore misplaced.

The lookup is now built for the misplaced tasks only. It still walks every
target standby placement once, but a placement of any other task no
longer creates a task ID, a map entry and a set, and a subtopology with no
misplaced task is skipped after a single map lookup.

KAFKA-21273: Patch the refiner's intermediate assignment copy-on-write

assemble() patches the members whose tasks a staged migration, a warm-up
task or a withheld standby changes. PatchedTasks copied all three roles
of such a member in full, every partition set included, although a patch
changes one task at a time.

A role is now copied only when a patch first changes it, and within a
role only the partition sets a patch changes are copied; the others stay
shared with the target assignment, which nothing mutates. A set that is
still the target assignment's own object is told apart by identity and
copied before it changes. A subtopology whose last partition a patch
removes is still dropped, and a later patch that adds one back starts a
new set.

This reduces what a refinement allocates; the intermediate assignment is
unchanged.

KAFKA-21273: Keep the refiner's borrowed and parked migrations in hash sets

planWarmups collected the borrowed and the parked migrations in TreeSets.
Nothing reads them in order: assemble asks the borrowed set whether it
contains each staged migration, indexStandbyConflicts walks it but keeps
the smallest member ID and fills a set, so the visiting order does not
matter, and nothing in the main code reads the parked set.

Both are now HashSets, so adding and looking up a migration take constant
time instead of time logarithmic in the number of migrations. The
intermediate assignment is unchanged.

KAFKA-21273: Count active tasks only where the refined assignment differs

When the refined assignment is not the target assignment itself,
AssignmentRefiner.preservesActiveTaskCount counted every active task of
every member in both. The built-in refiner hands every member it does not
patch back as the target assignment's own task tuple, so only the patched
members can change the count.

The check now adds up the difference over the members that can change it:
for each refined member whose tuple is not the target's own object, its
active tasks minus its target's, and for each target member missing from
the refined assignment, minus its active tasks. The difference of the two
totals is the sum of these terms, because a member whose tuple is the same
object contributes nothing, so the check accepts and rejects exactly the
same assignments as before.

KAFKA-21273: Index the refiner's state on disk only when it is asked for

The index walk read every member's offset reports for the misplaced
tasks, to record which process reports state for a task it holds no role
for. Only the case analysis reads that, for a misplaced task no member
holds as an active task, so most refinements built it for nothing.

StateOnDisk now builds that per-process lookup on the first question,
from the same reports and against the same holders and copies, which the
index has completed by then, and keeps it for the rest of the refinement.
A lookup is still a hash lookup, and the intermediate assignment is
unchanged.
